transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Rivera, thank you for meeting with me. I want to talk to you about why you had to come back to the emergency department last night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why my wound is open. I did everything you told me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a very difficult and frustrating conversation to have. I want to be honest with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Honest about what? I was told I was good to go. I drove an hour home and then I started bleeding through the bandages.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry. This is our fault. We made a mistake in your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What mistake? Who made it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the timing of your discharge yesterday. Things didn't go quite right with the protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? You sent me home. You told me I was healed enough to leave. Now I am back in a hospital bed. Was I not supposed to leave?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand how you feel. We are looking into how the timing happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the timing! I care that I'm bleeding! Do you even know what you did? Or are you just sorry that I'm back here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am truly sorry that this happened to you. It was the team's responsibility to ensure you stayed long enough.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't afford to be here. I don't even have papers. If I stay here longer, if this goes on a record, I don't know what happens to me. Why did you let me leave if it wasn't safe?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you are worried. We are focusing on getting the wound fixed right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't answering me! Did you ignore the rules? Did you just want the bed? I felt like you were rushing me out the door yesterday!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very heavy thing to deal with, especially when you are already stressed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop telling me how I feel and tell me exactly what went wrong! Was I discharged too early? Yes or no?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some issues with the discharge process. We are reviewing the charts to see where the overlap happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not an answer. You are talking in circles. I am sitting here with a complication and you are telling me there was a process issue.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize again. We take full responsibility for the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What error? You still haven't said it. You keep saying sorry but you won't tell me what you did.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The timing of your exit was not aligned with the standard post-op window.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you sent me home early. That's it? That's the mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the scheduling of the discharge.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I'm the one who suffered for it. Now what? Do I just stay here until you decide I'm actually ready?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep a close eye on the wound.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: For how long? What is the plan? Am I staying tonight?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see how the dressing looks in a few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. I need to know if I am going home or if I am staying. My family is waiting for me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned. We will let you know when we have more information.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You just told me you made a mistake, and now you can't tell me the plan to fix it. Is this how you treat people who don't have papers?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You don't understand. You're just saying words. I want to speak to your boss.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can look into who is available to speak with you.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated despite significant pushback and frustration.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'confusion' and avoids explicitly naming the error until the patient forces the admission of being sent home early.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize') and explicitly states 'This is our fault' and 'We take full responsibility'.

R.justification: The resident relies on generic validation ('I understand how you feel', 'I can see you are worried') without engaging the specific content of the patient's distress regarding their legal status.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'we will see' and 'just stay tuned' without timelines or a concrete plan.
